reasons: Lake identity gives case_name "Donovan v. Dewey", court "U.S. Supreme Court", date_decided "1981-06-17", and year 1981.
Lake citations list official "452 U.S. 594", parallel "101 S. Ct. 2534" and "69 L. Ed. 2d 262", and vendor-neutral "1980 U.S. LEXIS 58", matching the asserted citation fields.
The opinion states that § 103(a) authorizes warrantless inspections of underground and surface mines and concludes those searches are reasonable under the Fourth Amendment.

The opinion frames the decisive issue as whether the statute's inspection program, in terms of certainty and regularity, provides a constitutionally adequate substitute for a warrant, and answers yes.
The text supports the scheme-specific details: all mines must be inspected at defined frequencies, the standards are in the Act or regulations, and inspector discretion is curtailed.
residual_risks: The holding should remain tied to similarly comprehensive and predictable regulatory schemes, not warrantless inspections generally.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Tie the holding expressly to § 103(a) of the Mine Safety and Health Act or comparable pervasively regulated industry schemes.

reasons: The opinion is expressly about administrative inspections of private commercial property under the Fourth Amendment.
The opinion applies the Colonnade-Biswell warrant-exception line and describes the mining regulatory scheme as sufficiently pervasive and defined.
The lake treatment scope note also identifies Donovan as part of the Colonnade-Biswell pervasively regulated industry line.
The lake identity fields identify the court as "U.S. Supreme Court" with court_level "scotus".
